I think many would agree with me that, regardless of what game you play, you can feel what the devs’ intention is. Whether the game is good or not, some games are the devs trying to captivate you with their art and aesthetics. Some games are trying to sheepishly please you by giving you mechanics and tropes you’re familiar with. Some games try to impress you with the cool bosses, shocking moments, and exciting designs. Some beg you to be entertained, trying to occupy your time with so many elements such as organization, grinding, side quests, etc.

I didn’t think I would ever say this about any game ever, but Omnibus is a flex.  Omnibus doesn’t try; it just is. It doesn’t joke, hoping you would laugh. It’s a group of cool friends laughing amongst each other so candidly, you WANT to join in and be part of the fun. Omnibus doesn’t care. Omnibus doesn’t say “please like me”. It smirks and says “let me show you how it’s done.”

I know this sounds like a meme review, but I promise it isn’t. Omnibus is an easy game to enjoy, but an astronomically hard game to explain. I cannot even describe it as “whimsical and creative” because Omnibus is a redefinition of these very terms. It’s a one-of-a-kind experience, down to the smallest details.

I may not be able to explain Omnibus, but one thing is for certain; I doubt many people will regret playing it.

Ran great on the steam deck, despite being listed as untested. I'd consider this 'verified' quality. Problem is, when the rudimentary low poly aesthetic and occasional goat sim-esque cluster ♥♥♥♥ physics objects wears off, the game's amateurish design and gameplay are what remain. At it's core, omnibus is a rage game where the player is constantly fighting the many forces acting against your bus. I often found myself frequently fighting the spin and rapid velocity of the car or just restarting the level because the rate at which I careen off the platform is futile against any effort I put in. Many turns into pinball-like bumpers render a run unsalvageable. The controls go from a razor tight, lightspeed precision to floaty and hardly manipulatable. Attach it to a campaign of levels which serve as vignette segments with barely any sequential elements, and you have a game worth skipping. 

Some bus's have individual abilities, like the gravity bus, where pushing a button can influence the force of gravity pulling it's wheels to the ground. That kind of ability grants more and more unique moments of gameplay, but it never strives to take these individual powers and combine them. I wish, as a game, there should be a bus which requires you to jump with the cow ability, flip upside down, and use the gravity ledge to grab a hold of a drivable path to progress the game. But it never allowed itself the ambition to reach a moment where it felt distinct from some itch.io game for free. It's not worth it.

Despite what you may assume based on the look of it, this is no mere one-joke-rage-bait game. This is an objective based precision racing game that has both a good variety of missions and isn't overwhelmingly difficult. If you've ever played the mission mode in Mario Kart DS it's a bit like that, but you can't stop and the missions are more fleshed out. 

The game isn't very long so it doesn't overstay its welcome, and there's enough variety to keep surprising you and introducing new twists on the existing gameplay loop. As such for a Lincoln it's hard not to recommend.

If you're the casual type who doesn't go for achievements, this game isn't too hard. Even if its physics are dogwater and the levels can be annoying, there isn't anything you shouldn't be able to do. The game is hard but it isn't "I Wanna be the Guy" levels of hard. If you don't care about 100% and you want a fun, gimmicky game to pass the time, you might like this. It's got some charm and some nice ideas, plus all the levels are unique so you'll never see anything truly rehashed from previous areas. It's cheap, simple, and doesn't take too long. Isn't that nice?

NOW IF YOU'RE A COMPLETIONIST:

DO NOT. THERE ARE BETTER GAMES. I HAVE 100%'D THIS GAME AND IT'S A PIECE OF ♥♥♥♥.
No game has given me more heartache than when I lose my 6th cow, more dread than when I'm half a second off of gold, and NO GAME has instilled more stomach-churning regret than when I mess up at 39 chickens and need to restart again.

But it doesn't end there.

Some of the game's hats are especially ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrid to get. How would you like to perform physics equations about a spinning bridge in your little brain while your bus constantly changes forms and weight, causing you to just die because lol random? Isn't that great? What about using a slippery gravity control to aim with pin-point precision at a hat suspended in the air while going 150mph?

If you want to 100% this game, you are an idiot, and anyone who sees your suffering will be all entitled to laugh and jeer as you trip on a sign post and have to restart your chicken collectathon again.

Omnibus is a game made to annoy you, make you feel stupid. The grimy music loops gnaw away at your ear drums and the bright colourful visuals only juxtapose your torment. When you don't go for 100%, you don't realise this. You just think it's a product of its time and made to parody old and busted arcade games. It's only when you yearn for completion and load back in that you start to realise just how wrong you were.

But, I do like it.

[b]Avaliação do jogo: OmniBus[/b]

OmniBus é um jogo de aventura caótica onde você controla um ônibus desgovernado que deve enfrentar uma série de desafios absurdos. Nesta avaliação, exploraremos OmniBus como um título que oferece diversão frenética e humor sem limites.

[b]Caos sobre Rodas[/b]
Uma das características centrais do jogo é o caos constante, à medida que você tenta manter um ônibus descontrolado na estrada, realizando tarefas absurdas.

[b]Variedade de Desafios[/b]
OmniBus oferece uma variedade de desafios, desde pular rampas em alta velocidade até lançar carros pelos ares, mantendo o jogo sempre fresco.

[b]Humor Inigualável[/b]
O jogo é repleto de humor exagerado e situações absurdas que fazem você rir a cada momento.

[b]Estilo Visual Único[/b]
A estética do jogo, com gráficos simples e vibrantes, contribui para a experiência divertida e descontraída.

[b]Desafio Crescente[/b]
À medida que você avança, os desafios se tornam cada vez mais difíceis, exigindo reflexos rápidos e habilidades precisas.

[b]Conclusão[/b]
OmniBus é um jogo que não leva a sério a física ou a lógica, mas oferece uma montanha-russa de diversão caótica. Com seu caos sobre rodas, variedade de desafios, humor inigualável, estilo visual único e desafios crescentes, o jogo é uma experiência única e hilária.
